subject: Whole deleted terminal passages now fade for at least 450ms, with the approved Standard and Intrusive defaults ready in a native testing instance.
reader: Parker, who just selected these lighting values from native GAUGES screenshots and asked for complete deleted words and paragraphs to linger as the cursor moves.

sections.heading: Deleted text now lingers
sections.text:
You wanted the whole deleted word or paragraph to remain on the glass as the cursor moves away. The new build keeps those old letters at their previous positions for a longer fade, and uses the Standard and Intrusive defaults from your screenshots. 

450 ms 
Minimum fade for erased text. Ordinary replacements start at 220 ms. New text appears immediately.

legend.0: Nothing. Every term the passage leans on is either ordinary English or is explained in the passage at the point it is first used. The reader follows it from the first sentence to the last without stopping.
legend.1: One or two things are named without being explained — a file, a component, a product — but the sentences around them make their role clear enough that the reader keeps going without losing the thread.
legend.2: Several names or terms arrive unexplained, so the reader follows the argument only by taking them on trust.
legend.3: The passage is written for somebody already inside the project. Its central sentences cannot be understood at all without knowledge the document has not supplied anywhere.

sections.heading: The whole passage stays
sections.text:
These are recorded frames from the native terminal. The left pane erased its text; the cursor moved about 60 ms later. The untouched pane beside it changed by zero pixels. Choose the paragraph or word, then compare the three captures. 
 01 · NATIVE ERASURE 
 Wrapped paragraph Whole word 
Capture began 258 ms after erasure 
 Early After 220 ms Finished 
 Figure 1. The complete visible deletion survives cursor movement and the shorter replacement fade. Capture began around 258 ms after erasure; the image takes another 140–150 ms to capture. The word and paragraph both remain visible, with less light than in their early frames. The finished captures begin around 650 ms. Deterministic tests verify expiry at 450 ms. Letter bloom is disabled in this timing fixture to isolate the retained glyphs. measured

sections.heading: The dial controls the fade
sections.text:
The existing Afterglow slider stays at 220 ms by default. Erased text uses the longer of that value and 450 ms. Set the slider to zero to clear all afterglow, or raise it above 450 ms to lengthen both kinds. 
 02 · DRAWING RULE 
 Figure 2. The longer erasure fade never delays current text. This timeline is drawn from Trail::observe , not from a frame-time measurement. Each pane retains at most the larger of one visible viewport and 4,096 glyphs. Bottom alignment alone preserves the old coordinates; scrolling, resizing, changing focus or theme still clears them. code-derived

sections.heading: Your two defaults
sections.text:
The organised GAUGES now resolve unset lighting controls from the selected design. Existing values you explicitly set keep priority. Both modes use 100% inactive glow and the shared picture settings in your screenshots. 
 03 · NATIVE GAUGES 

 STANDARD 20% active glow · 45% inactive text 

 INTRUSIVE 37% active glow · 52% inactive text 
 Figure 3. Both native panels show the defaults you selected. The lighting fields were absent in both fixture files. Inactive text is a fraction of the active text-intensity setting, not a measured luminance ratio. New windows also start with the shared picture values shown here; older saved grades retain their compatibility values. measured

sections.heading: Try it in your window
sections.text:
The separate test instance is open on workspace 4 . Select ERASED TEXT · 220 / 450 ms : the left shell uses Standard and the right uses Intrusive. Click between them to compare focus, then run: 
afterglow-demo 
The demo alternates ordinary replacement, whole-word deletion and a wrapped-paragraph deletion with cursor movement. Ctrl+C returns to the original screen. Your four earlier shells and their contents remain in the other tabs. Close GAUGES to see GPU letter glow; the existing panel-preview limitation remains. 

 Deleted-text readability 
The erasure fade starts at 450 ms. Try deleting your own words and paragraphs, and leave a note here if the trail should stay stronger or linger longer. 

 Verification and source 
Both full core suites passed: 2,612 / 2,559 tests , with 10 ignored in each. Both strict Clippy gates, format and the locked release build passed. New tests cover complete deleted strings, cursor movement, exact expiry, a viewport larger than the old cap and design defaults surviving a palette change. | 
 | Native check | Result 
 | Word and paragraph beyond 220 ms | Visible old glyphs remain; the neighboring text region is identical. 
 | Ordinary replacement after 220 ms | Within one 8-bit RGB level of the settled frame. Timing starts at output emission, not the first rendered frame. 
 | Erasure with afterglow zero | Early and settled text regions match exactly. 
 | Live delivery | Six interactive panes, including the four earlier shell processes; the running executable matches the tested release binary. 
An erasure is detected when any painted row loses visible graphemes. Every changed old glyph in that update receives the longer lifetime. This covers wrapped passages and prompt movement without inspecting an editor's key commands. Restoring a heading on another row cannot cancel the erasure. 
The larger fresh text default exposed a clipped startup grid in the test fixture. Only its window height changed from 640 to 720 pixels; its intentional 100×28 grid and interaction assertions remain intact. 
Evidence: native timing · pixel comparisons · test counts · running instance . GPU frame cost remains unmeasured qualification work ; the GAUGES preview limitation is separately tracked. 
Source: glyph retention · painted coordinates · defaults . Binary SHA-256: 81eb231005af6354ed33645988a517ef646549f4ebdad566ed22cd245e9a4a06 .
